name: ADS1015 12-bit 4-channel ADC
description: Texas Instruments 12-bit delta-sigma ADC with 4 single-ended (or 2 differential) inputs, a programmable gain amplifier (FSR +/-6.144 V to +/-0.256 V, 3 mV to 0.125 mV per LSB) and up to 3300 samples/s, read over I2C. Runs on 2.0-5.5 V. Sold as: Adafruit ADS1015 12-Bit ADC breakout (#1083, original 10-pin single-row version), 10-pin header VDD, GND, SCL, SDA, ADDR, ALRT, A0, A1, A2, A3, I2C address 0x48 (ADDR to VDD/SDA/SCL for 0x49/0x4A/0x4B).
eli5: Gives your board four extra, more precise analog inputs: it measures voltages and sends the numbers over two wires.

pins.name: VDD
pins.description: Supply and I/O level, 2.0-5.5 V (use 3.3 V with an ESP32 or Pico)

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (10 k pull-up to VDD on the board)

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (10 k pull-up to VDD on the board)

pins.name: ADDR
pins.description: Address select (10 k pull-down): GND/open = 0x48, VDD = 0x49, SDA = 0x4A, SCL = 0x4B

pins.name: ALRT
pins.description: ALERT/RDY open-drain output (10 k pull-up), comparator or conversion-ready; not needed for basic use

pins.name: A0
pins.description: Analog input AIN0, GND to VDD (never above VDD + 0.3 V)

pins.name: A1
pins.description: Analog input AIN1, GND to VDD

pins.name: A2
pins.description: Analog input AIN2, GND to VDD

pins.name: A3
pins.description: Analog input AIN3, GND to VDD

supplierQuery: ADS1015 12-bit 4 channel I2C ADC breakout module
buildNotes: Single-shot read: write the Config register (pointer 0x01) with OS=1, the MUX input, PGA range, MODE=1 and data rate; wait 1/DR (0.625 ms at 1600 SPS) or until OS reads back 1; then read the Conversion register (pointer 0x00).
The 12-bit result is two's complement, left-justified in bits 15:4: code = signed16 >> 4, volts = code x FSR / 2048 (2 mV per count at +/-4.096 V, 1 mV at the default +/-2.048 V).
Inputs must stay between GND and VDD (absolute max VDD + 0.3 V) whatever FSR you pick; +/-4.096 V is the useful range on a 3.3 V supply.
ADDR has a 10 k pull-down on the board: leave it open for 0x48; tie it to VDD, SDA or SCL for 0x49, 0x4A or 0x4B (up to four boards on one bus).
Power VDD from the same 3.3 V as the microcontroller: the board's SDA/SCL pull-ups go to VDD.

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from ads1015 import ADS1015

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
adc = ADS1015(i2c, fsr=4.096)
while True:
    print('A0=%.3fV' % adc.read_voltage(0))
    time.sleep(1)
